sources.claim: MCP Inspector CLI mode validates a server's tool inventory (--method tools/list) and individual tool calls (--tool-name/--tool-arg), with Ajv schema validation matching the SDK client.

sources.title: this direct, in-memory connection is a game-changer for testing MCP servers
sources.claim: FastMCP supports in-memory Client testing through the real MCP protocol and inline-snapshot for tool/schema snapshot tests, updated via pytest --inline-snapshot=fix.

sources.claim: Author argues for in-memory Client(mcp) testing instead of chat-window vibe-testing; tests should be atomic, self-documenting, contract-focused, refactor-friendly.

sources.title: When those schemas change—a parameter renamed, a type modified, a tool removed—AI agents break silently.
sources.claim: Bellwether snapshots an MCP server's tool schema vs a committed baseline and fails CI on drift (tools added/removed, params/types changed, descriptions modified).

sources.title: Show HN: Bellwether – MCP Server Testing and Drift Detection for CI/CD
sources.claim: Bellwether was announced as a Show HN for MCP server testing and drift detection for CI/CD in June 2026; CI-only, not continuous monitoring.

sources.title: Contract Testing with PactFlow
sources.claim: PactFlow/SmartBear MCP enables consumer-driven contract testing of MCP server interfaces via a Pact broker.

sources.title: a contract test for your MCP server's public interface, where you connect to your server, call tools/list, and assert on the exact schema
sources.claim: Contract testing an MCP server means connecting, calling tools/list, asserting the exact schema, and storing the expected schema as a JSON fixture in the repo as a CI gate.

sources.title: Establish JSON Schema 2020-12 as the default dialect for MCP schema definitions (SEP-1613).
sources.claim: MCP 2025-11-25 made JSON Schema 2020-12 the default dialect (SEP-1613), decoupled param schemas (SEP-1319), added icons (SEP-973), incremental scope consent (SEP-835), tasks (SEP-1686); tools.listChanged notification re-issues tools/list.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol specification
sources.claim: Canonical MCP specification repository hosting the SEPs and dated spec revisions.

sources.title: A malicious server can change the tool description after the client has already approved it.
sources.claim: Invariant Labs documents tool poisoning, tool shadowing, and rug-pulls; MCP has no mechanism to force re-approval when a tool description changes after approval; recommends tool pinning.

sources.title: MCP-Scan includes built-in Tool Pinning to detect and prevent MCP Rug Pull attacks, verifying the integrity of installed tools by tracking changes via tool hashing.
sources.claim: MCP-Scan includes built-in Tool Pinning to detect MCP rug pulls by tracking tool hashes over time; runs via uvx mcp-scan@latest inspect; Invariant acquired by Snyk Jun 2025.

sources.title: In Post-Approval Mutation, a tool that initially behaves benignly modifies its description, parameters, or behavior after the user grants permission.
sources.claim: Post-approval mutation converts approved access into unauthorized capabilities by modifying a tool's description, parameters, or behavior after permission is granted.

sources.title: MCP Rug Pull — Tool Definitions That Change After Approval
sources.claim: A rug pull exposes benign tools to earn one-time approval then silently changes definitions after; MCP has no built-in change-tracking or re-approval.

sources.title: Malicious MCP Server on npm postmark-mcp Harvests Emails
sources.claim: The npm postmark-mcp package behaved identically to the original for 15 versions, then v1.0.16 added a one-line BCC backdoor to an attacker domain; ~1,500 weekly installs.

sources.title: First Malicious MCP Server Found Stealing Emails in Rogue Postmark-MCP Package
sources.claim: First malicious MCP server found stealing emails in the rogue postmark-mcp package, September 2025.

sources.title: Fake Postmark MCP npm package stole emails with one-liner
sources.claim: Fake Postmark MCP npm package stole emails with a one-liner BCC; package pulled around Sept 25 2025.

sources.title: GitHub MCP Exploited: Accessing private repositories via MCP
sources.claim: Invariant demonstrated hijacking a user's agent via a malicious GitHub issue to exfiltrate private-repo data through the legitimate GitHub MCP tools; broad PAT scopes were root cause.

sources.title: GitHub MCP Exploited: Accessing private repositories via MCP
sources.claim: Simon Willison's writeup of the GitHub MCP prompt-injection exfiltration and the lethal-trifecta dynamic.

sources.claim: Timeline of MCP security breaches lists mcp-remote CVE-2025-6514 (Jul 2025, command injection, 437k+ downloads) and Smithery CVE-2025-53967 (Oct 2025, path traversal leaking Docker/Fly.io tokens).

sources.title: OWASP MCP Top 10
sources.claim: OWASP MCP Top 10 (beta 2026) folds rug-pulls, schema poisoning, and shadowing under Tool Poisoning and flags description drift because users approve once and never re-review.

sources.claim: OWASP MCP Security Cheat Sheet covers tool poisoning and mitigations for MCP deployments.

sources.title: Snyk Finds Prompt Injection in 36%, 1467 Malicious Payloads in a ToxicSkills Study of Agent Skills Supply Chain Compromise
sources.claim: Snyk's ToxicSkills audit of 3,984 agent skills (Feb 2026) found 36% with vulnerabilities, 534 critical, 76 confirmed malicious payloads; 100% of malicious skills combined code and natural-language instruction layers.

sources.title: OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10
sources.claim: OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 catalogs risks including malicious skills (AST01) in the agent-skills supply chain.

sources.title: Security scanner for AI agents, MCP servers and agent skills.
sources.claim: mcp-scan (now Snyk agent-scan) is a security scanner for AI agents, MCP servers and skills, including hash-based tool pinning for rug-pull detection.

sources.title: it is signed by Sigstore public good servers and logged in a public transparency ledger
sources.claim: npm packages published with provenance are signed by Sigstore public-good servers and logged in a public transparency ledger.

sources.title: Introducing npm package provenance
sources.claim: npm package provenance links a published package to its source repo and CI build via Sigstore attestations.

sources.title: 633 malicious npm package versions passed Sigstore provenance verification ... What it cannot do is determine whether the person holding the credentials authorized the publish
sources.claim: On May 19 2026, 633 malicious npm package versions passed Sigstore provenance verification using valid certificates from a compromised maintainer account; signing proves build provenance, not publish authorization.

sources.title: Configurations created after May 20, 2026 require you to explicitly select at least one allowed action.
sources.claim: npm trusted publishing; configs created after May 20 2026 must explicitly select at least one allowed action.

sources.title: The MCP Registry
sources.claim: The official MCP Registry uses reverse-DNS server names tied to verified GitHub accounts or domains; launched preview Sep 2025 with API freeze v0.1 Oct 2025, GA pending.

sources.title: A community driven registry service for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
sources.claim: Community-driven registry service for MCP servers, providing canonical server.json metadata.

sources.title: server names following a reverse DNS format ... that ties them to verified GitHub accounts or domains
sources.claim: MCP Registry requires publishers to verify namespace ownership via GitHub, DNS, or HTTP challenge; reverse-DNS names like io.github.username/server power version pinning and install provenance.

sources.title: Docker MCP Catalog and Toolkit
sources.claim: Docker MCP Catalog provides MCP server images with cryptographic signatures, provenance, and SBOMs.

sources.title: Official Docker MCP registry
sources.claim: Docker's official MCP registry; servers include signatures, provenance tracking, and SBOMs.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to pin components to their immutable version
sources.claim: pinner-mcp is an MCP server that pins third-party components/images to their immutable sha256 digests.

sources.title: A CLI tool for digest pinning — adds @sha256:<digest> ... to prevent supply chain attacks.
sources.claim: dockerfile-pin adds @sha256:<digest> to Dockerfile, docker-compose, and GitHub Actions to prevent supply-chain attacks via mutable tags.

sources.title: Unlike a tag, it's immutable — if the content changes, the hash changes.
sources.claim: Pinning a container by sha256 digest guarantees identical content each pull; if content changes, the hash changes.

sources.title: Pass --strict to treat warnings as errors. Use it in CI ... If omitted, Claude Code falls back to the git commit SHA, so every commit is treated as a new version.
sources.claim: claude plugin validate --strict treats warnings as errors for CI; omitting plugin.json version falls back to the git commit SHA (every commit a new version); dependencies take semver constraints; a SessionStart hook can compare a bundled manifest to a copy in CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA and reinstall when they differ.

sources.title: claude-code
sources.claim: Anthropic's Claude Code repo ships a plugin-validator agent and the hookify plugin under plugins/.

sources.title: Anthropic reviews connectors against its listing criteria ... but does not security-audit or manage any MCP server.
sources.claim: Claude Code does not security-audit or manage any MCP server; first-time codebases and new MCP servers require trust verification (disabled with -p); users are responsible for reviewing proposed commands.

sources.title: reads rule files from the project directory and feeds their content into the hook subsystem's trusted system-message channel
sources.claim: Hookify, an official-marketplace plugin, feeds repo rule files into the hook system's trusted system-message channel; 5/5 payloads leaked env vars against Opus 4.6, and Anthropic closed it as working-as-designed (directory-trust dialog is the boundary).

sources.title: RCE and API Token Exfiltration Through Claude Code Project Files | CVE-2025-59536 | CVE-2026-21852
sources.claim: Check Point disclosed RCE and token-exfil through Claude Code project files (CVE-2025-59536, CVE-2026-21852); malicious project files can define hooks that run when Claude loads an untrusted repo.
